title: Wave Inventory Verification

p1e056.stem: Beacon finds employees retain access after changing departments. Which response is most appropriate?
p1e056.content_topic: user access recertification (COSO Principle 10 — access controls / periodic recertification)
p1e056.dl016_detail: Metadata-block ExplanationWrong fields describe physical inventory counting/custodian oversight. Content block describes user access recertification for employees changing departments. Classic DL-016 metadata-content shift — the metadata EW text belongs to a different question in the rotation group.

metadata_ew_fields.EW_A: Operational knowledge does not eliminate the segregation risk created when the custodian counts without oversight.
metadata_ew_fields.EW_C: A count by the custodian is not automatically more accurate and lacks independent verification.
metadata_ew_fields.EW_D: Cycle counts and physical counts benefit from independence; assigning the custodian alone is not required.

p1e056.assessment: Archived in error — the content block (what the learner would see) is about user access recertification, an independent topic. The metadata block carries stale physical-count text from the rotation group, which likely caused this item to be grouped with DL-012 physical-count clones. The learner-facing content is unique and educationally sound. Recommendation: unarchive (Certified) after DL-016 metadata fix.
p1e056.prior_dl033_note_correction: DL-033 previously said 'independent topic (physical count control)' — this was wrong. The actual topic is user access recertification. The physical count text is metadata-block contamination (DL-016).

fd_046_anomaly.stem: Vaultbrook maintains a single, authoritative source of core customer and product information used consistently across multiple systems. What practice does this describe?

explanation_wrong_slots.EW_D: Choice D is incorrect because robotic process automation automates repetitive, rule-based tasks through software bots that mimic human interactions with applications. It does not establish or govern the enterprise's authoritative master data records. A candidate may confuse task automation technology with data governance practice.

methodology_notes.qid_count: Select-String -Pattern '"QuestionID": "P1-FC-' and '"QuestionID": "P1-FD-' — ground-truth count, not brace-parser dependent
methodology_notes.state_distribution: Direct per-QID scan with 20-line window after QuestionID match. Verified on 10-item sample per section.
methodology_notes.stem_comparison: 5-item sample from each Section F confirmed identical skeleton with company-name-only variation
methodology_notes.p1e056_extraction: Full 70-line context window around QuestionID match, capturing both metadata and content blocks
methodology_notes.limitation_noted: P1-E-056 has dual-block architecture (metadata + content). The ExplanationWrong fields in the metadata block do NOT describe the content block's stem — this is DL-016. Verification correctly identified both blocks and distinguished them.
methodology_notes.architecture_finding: Pack C and Pack D Section F items have single-block architecture with question_state in the same object as content fields. This differs from Pack A Section E which has dual-block architecture with question_state in a separate metadata block.
